note: BCMA (TNFRSF17) depleters — CAR-T (ide-cel, orva-cel, P-BCMA-101, AUTO2), the ADC belantamab mafodotin and CD3 bispecifics — all entered relapsed/refractory myeloma on BCMA+ xenografts in NSG mice, which lack a human immune compartment and so cannot show cytokine release syndrome or neurotoxicity.
label: Myeloma (BCMA)

engagement.model: BCMA+ myeloma xenografts (H929, RPMI-8226) in NSG mice
engagement.note: First anti-BCMA CAR: T cells recognised BCMA specifically and eradicated myeloma xenografts in immunodeficient mice; no patient read-out yet.
engagement.short: First anti-BCMA CAR clears mouse xenografts
engagement.quote: The CARs gave T cells the ability to specifically recognize BCMA.

engagement.model: BCMA+ myeloma xenografts (H929, RPMI-8226) in NSG mice
engagement.note: In the first-in-human trial, BCMA+ bone-marrow plasma cells became undetectable after CAR-BCMA T cells, the on-target depletion the mouse predicted.
engagement.short: Marrow plasma cells cleared in patients
engagement.quote: After treatment, bone marrow plasma cells became undetectable by flow cytometry, and the patient's MM entered a stringent complete remission that lasted for 17 weeks before relapse.
engagement.reason: Plasma cells cleared as model said
engagement.judgement: Engagement read as BCMA+ plasma-cell depletion (the model's claim was BCMA-specific killing). Abstract-level; no source puts model and patient engagement side by side. Soluble-BCMA elimination after ide-cel is reported in the FDA Abecma review (2021, https://www.fda.gov/media/147627/download) but likewise without a model comparison.

dose.model: BCMA+ myeloma xenografts (H929, RPMI-8226) in NSG mice
dose.note: Mouse CAR-T doses were proof-of-concept only; no exposure or cell-dose target was carried from the xenograft into patients.
dose.short: Mouse doses set no human target
dose.quote: The anti-BCMA-CAR-transduced T cells exhibited BCMA-specific functions including cytokine production, proliferation, cytotoxicity, and in vivo tumor eradication.

dose.model: Patient bone-marrow ex vivo cytotoxicity (EC50–EC90) + PK simulation (teclistamab)
dose.note: Ex vivo EC90 from patient marrow set a 0.72 mg/kg SC floor; 0.72 and 1.5 mg/kg were the active clinical doses.
dose.short: Ex vivo EC90 matched active doses
dose.quote: Thus, a PK modeling approach using preclinical and initial clinical data successfully predicted clinically active doses of teclistamab.
dose.reason: Ex vivo EC90 held at active doses
dose.judgement: The model is an ex vivo potency assay on patient marrow (first reported Pillarisetti 2020, https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2020002393) coupled to human PK, not an animal. The same paper's cynomolgus arm mismatched patients on marrow:serum ratio (0.3–0.6 vs >=1) but the dose never relied on it. CAR-T and ADC doses in this class were empirical escalations with no published exposure-target comparison. MajesTEC-1 (NCT03145181) has no registry results posted as of 2026-11-02.

efficacy.model: BCMA+ myeloma xenografts (H929, RPMI-8226) in NSG mice
efficacy.note: Anti-BCMA CAR T cells eradicated established human myeloma xenografts in immunodeficient mice; no patient comparison existed.
efficacy.quote: The anti-BCMA-CAR-transduced T cells exhibited BCMA-specific functions including cytokine production, proliferation, cytotoxicity, and in vivo tumor eradication.

efficacy.model: BCMA+ myeloma xenografts (H929, RPMI-8226) in NSG mice
efficacy.note: First-in-human CAR-BCMA produced a stringent complete remission at the top dose, as the xenograft predicted, but it lasted 17 weeks.
efficacy.quote: Our findings demonstrate antimyeloma activity of CAR-BCMA T cells.
efficacy.judgement: Direction held for every agent that reached patients (bb2121 ORR 85%, Raje 2019 doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1817226; ide-cel 73%, Munshi 2021 doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2024850; belantamab 31–34%, Lonial 2020 doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(19)30788-0), but the model's tumour eradication never translated (median PFS 8.8–11.8 months), so magnitude is direction_only. Borderline case NOT scored as contra: AUTO2 (APRIL-CAR) cleared xenografts in Lee 2018 (doi:10.1182/blood-2017-05-781351) yet gave 4/11 responders and was terminated for insufficient efficacy (NCT03287804, results posted 2020-10-23) — a magnitude miss, not a direction reversal, and only a registry record documents it. model_filed=true because the FDA Abecma review names a xenograft murine model as ide-cel's in vivo proof of concept.

safety.model: BCMA+ myeloma xenografts in NSG mice (no human immune system)
safety.note: NSG xenografts carry no human myeloid or cytokine compartment, so the model was silent on cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity.
safety.quote: Except for expression in plasma cells, BCMA protein was not detected in normal human tissues.

safety.model: BCMA+ myeloma xenografts in NSG mice (no human immune system)
safety.note: Both patients at the active dose had cytokine release syndrome, which a mouse without human immune cells could not show.
safety.short: CRS in patients, unseen in mice
safety.quote: Both patients treated on the fourth dose level had toxicity consistent with cytokine-release syndrome including fever, hypotension, and dyspnea.
safety.judgement: Model silence that did not hold: CRS later 76% with 42% neurotoxicity (Raje 2019) and 84–85% with 18–28% neurotoxicity under a REMS (Munshi 2021; FDA Abecma review 2021, which lists no animal toxicology beyond the xenograft). ADC arm is mixed and not scored separately: EMA's Blenrep EPAR (EMA/CHMP/414341/2020) states corneal effects 'were seen in rats and rabbits, but not in monkeys', while DREAMM-2 (Lonial 2020; NCT03525678 results 2020-04-28) reported grade 3–4 keratopathy in 27%; the rat and rabbit reports are dated 2018, i.e. partly post hoc. magnitude null because the model made no prediction to scale.
